title: Average Speed vs Average Velocity
subject: Physics
objective: Walk 4 km to school and back in an hour: average speed 4 km/h, average velocity zero. One uses total distance, the other displacement.

fill.q: For a round trip, average velocity is ____.
|Average velocity| is always ____ than or equal to average speed.

tf.q: For a round trip, average speed is zero.
tf.explain: Distance is non-zero, so average speed is non-zero.

tf.q: Average speed for two equal distances at 4 km/h and 12 km/h is 8 km/h.
tf.explain: Total time matters: it is 6 km/h.

tf.q: Average velocity can be zero while the object moved.
tf.explain: If it returns to the start.
It uses distance, which has no direction.

ar.a: For a round trip, average velocity is zero.
ar.r: Average velocity = total displacement ÷ total time.
ar.explain: Displacement is zero, so R explains A.

ar.a: Average speed of 30 km/h and 60 km/h over equal distances is 45 km/h.
ar.r: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
ar.explain: A is false (it is 40 km/h); R is the correct rule.

num.q: A car goes 60 km at 30 km/h and returns 60 km at 60 km/h. Find average speed and average velocity.
A student walks 600 m to school in 10 min and returns in 15 min. Find the average speed for the round trip in m/s.

short.q: Why can't we just average two speeds?
short.solution: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. At the lower speed you spend more time, so it counts more; a simple average ignores this.

short.q: A bus goes 60 km at 30 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. Find average speed and average velocity.
short.solution: Time = 2 h + 1 h = 3 h; distance 120 km; average speed 40 km/h. Displacement 0, so average velocity 0.

match.explain: Averages are always totals divided by total time.
